messages.content:
Browser automation error: 
switch_tab reports success but the page is still the file listing — the known bug.

## What happened

- You reported the known `switch_tab` bug: the tool says it switched but the page the AI (and the live view) works on is still the file listing.
- I traced the whole path in `api/`: `browse_action` → `runtime.run_tabs` → `tabs.switch_tab` → `browser.page`.

## What I did

- **Confirmed in source** (`api/codx/junior/browser/tabs.py:341,532`): `_activate()` reassigns `browser.page`, calls `bring_to_front()` and syncs `session.current_url/current_title`; `switch_tab` validates the index, activates, returns the descriptor. `runtime.run_tabs` (runtime.py:583-599) also drops `self._prefetch` and reschedules it, and `_cached_prefetch` refuses a snapshot whose URL differs from `browser.page.url`.
- **Ruled out** the two plausible causes on this tree: a silently dropped page object, and a stale prefetch snapshot of the old tab being served as the "page" after the switch.
- **Added** `api/tests/browser/test_tabs_switch.py` (5 tests, fake Playwright pages): switch moves `browser.page` and the session URL, active flags flip from the listing tab, `index=None` keeps the tab, out-of-range/non-numeric indices raise and leave the current tab untouched.
- **Not reproduced live**: `start_session` timed out twice (120 s) in this environment, so there is no runtime evidence yet — the symptom most likely comes from the served live view / a running image older than this source, not from the switch code itself.

## Demo

`api/tests/browser/test_tabs_switch.py` — QA run: **5 passed, 0 failed** (`pytest:api`).

## Next tasks

- `quick` — start a browser session, open two tabs (file listing + docs), run `switch_tab` and capture `browser_status` + `tabs` + screenshot to see whether the *page brief* or only the *VNC view* is stale.
- `quick` — if the live view is the stale part, fix the UI/VNC tab-focus sync (client) instead of the switch code.
- `max` — add a runtime-level test that asserts `run_tabs("switch_tab")` invalidates the prefetch cache (needs a runtime fixture).

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok` ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

"""
Tab (page) management for the shared browser session.

The browser container is a real Chromium window: the user watches it through the
live VNC view while the AI drives it over CDP, so tabs are a **shared** resource.
Opening, selecting and closing them must be visible in that same window.

``Browser`` (``codx.junior.browser.browser``) owns the connection and the page
automation primitives; this module adds the tab primitives it deliberately does
not cover, operating on a connected ``Browser``:

    tabs = await list_tabs(browser)         # every tab + active flag
    tab  = await open_tab(browser, url)     # new tab, navigated and focused
    tab  = await switch_tab(browser, index) # move the AI (and the user) to it
    tab  = await close_tab(browser, index)  # close one, activate the next

Keep-alive tab
--------------
Chromium exits when its **last window closes**, and the container keeps running
(the desktop session is still alive), so the live view stays up while the
browser window is gone: neither the user nor the AI can reach the page again
until the browser process is restarted.

To make that impossible by accident, every session owns one **keep-alive tab**
(``about:blank#codx-keep-alive``, titled "codx-junior · keep this tab open"):

- ``ensure_keep_alive_tab`` creates it once and reactivates the working tab, so
  closing every other tab leaves the window (and Chromium) alive;
- ``close_tab`` refuses to close it;
- ``ensure_page`` reopens a page when, despite the guard, the browser ends up
  with no tabs at all (see ``BrowserManager.connect_browser`` for the full
  recovery of a dead browser).

Conventions
-----------
- the *tab index* is the position of the page in ``context.pages`` (stable while
  no tab is opened or closed); that is what the agent tools expose;
- ``browser.page`` always points at the tab the AI drives;
- every selection is brought to front, so the live view shows the tab the AI is
  working on (co-browsing);
- the keep-alive tab and the last tab are never closed: closing them would close
  the browser window the user is watching.

"""
Tests for ``switch_tab``: the tab the AI drives must follow the selection.

A reported symptom was "switch_tab reports success but the page is still the file
listing": the command layer is what decides whether the AI drives the tab it
selected, so these tests pin the contract with fake Playwright pages (no browser
needed):

- the returned descriptor is the selected tab, flagged ``active``;
- ``browser.page`` (what every later action and the live view follow) points at
  it, not at the previous one;
- ``list_tabs`` agrees, so the tab strip the user watches shows the same state.
"""

import asyncio

import pytest

from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs


class _FakeSession:
    """Minimal BrowserSession stand-in (only the fields the tab layer touches)."""

    def __init__(self, current_url=None):
        self.id = "12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-ddddeeeeffff"
        self.current_url = current_url
        self.current_title = None

    def mark_active(self):
        pass


class _FakePage:
    def __init__(self, url="about:blank", title="", context=None):
        self.url = url
        self._title = title
        self._closed = False
        self.context = context
        self.brought_to_front = 0

    async def title(self):
        return self._title

    def is_closed(self):
        return self._closed

    async def bring_to_front(self):
        self.brought_to_front += 1

    async def close(self):
        self._closed = True
        if self.context and self in self.context.pages:
            self.context.pages.remove(self)


class _FakeContext:
    def __init__(self, pages=None):
        self.pages = list(pages or [])

    async def new_page(self):
        page = _FakePage(context=self)
        self.pages.append(page)
        return page


class _FakeBrowser:
    """Connected Browser double: ``page`` is the tab the AI drives."""

    def __init__(self, pages):
        self.context = _FakeContext(pages)
        for page in pages:
            page.context = self.context
        self.page = pages[0]
        self.session = _FakeSession(current_url=pages[0].url)


def _run(coroutine):
    return asyncio.run(coroutine)


def _listing():
    return _FakePage(url="file:///home/project/", title="File listing")


def _docs():
    return _FakePage(url="https://docs.test/start", title="Docs")


def _other():
    return _FakePage(url="https://other.test/", title="Other")


def test_switch_tab_moves_the_ai_to_the_selected_tab():
    listing, docs = _listing(), _docs()
    browser = _FakeBrowser([listing, docs])

    descriptor = _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 1))

    assert descriptor["index"] == 1
    assert descriptor["url"] == "https://docs.test/start"
    assert descriptor["title"] == "Docs"
    assert descriptor["active"] is True
    # The next action (and the live view) follows browser.page.
    assert browser.page is docs
    assert docs.brought_to_front == 1
    assert browser.session.current_url == "https://docs.test/start"


def test_switch_tab_flips_the_active_flags_from_the_listing():
    listing, docs, other = _listing(), _docs(), _other()
    browser = _FakeBrowser([listing, docs, other])
    _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 0))

    _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 2))

    tabs = _run(browser_tabs.list_tabs(browser))
    assert [tab["active"] for tab in tabs] == [False, False, True]
    assert [tab["url"] for tab in tabs] == [
        "file:///home/project/",
        "https://docs.test/start",
        "https://other.test/",
    ]


def test_switch_tab_without_index_keeps_the_current_tab():
    listing, docs = _listing(), _docs()
    browser = _FakeBrowser([listing, docs])
    _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 1))

    descriptor = _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser))

    assert descriptor["index"] == 1
    assert browser.page is docs


def test_switch_tab_rejects_an_index_out_of_range():
    browser = _FakeBrowser([_listing(), _docs()])

    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as error:
        _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 5))

    assert "out of range (0-1)" in str(error.value)
    assert browser.page is browser.context.pages[0]


def test_switch_tab_rejects_a_non_numeric_index():
    browser = _FakeBrowser([_listing(), _docs()])

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, "the docs one"))
